blocks.text: Install the root module first. Each section is independently runnable and uses the code from its matching website case.

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/plugin-host

blocks.text: Shared parameters: defineHost requires host constructor options. Nested execution.mutationTimeoutMs and execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs are required without defaults, bounding active mutation and pipeline draining. Both are 5000 ms here; false waits without a deadline. Omitted pipeline.mode is sync. Omitted domainCore returns an empty object, and omitted custom dispose uses core structured cleanup.

sections.heading: Install a plugin and read its extension

blocks.text: An application needs to add a named capability and later release its resources. Consumers need a usable extension after installation, rather than a partially initialized plugin object.

Assigning plugin methods directly onto an object does not define when installation commits or who owns cleanup. Returning before an asynchronous installer finishes also exposes methods before their resources exist.

defineHost creates the lifecycle owner, and await host.use() returns the installed registration. Both execution budgets are required and set to 5000 ms here; they have no implicit defaults. Dispose the host after use.

definePlugin requires the nonempty name greeting and an install callback returning an ordinary extension object. greet is a plugin-defined no-argument method returning a string. host.use takes a plugin batch and returns handles in input order.
Output:

blocks.code: hello

blocks.text: Prints `hello`. The registration extension is called only after the installation promise has completed, and the final await waits for host cleanup.

The handle owns host operations; the plugin owns the extension it installs. mutationTimeoutMs bounds active mutations and pipelineDrainTimeoutMs bounds shutdown draining; false explicitly removes either deadline. These limits do not preempt user JavaScript.

sections.heading: Roll back a failed batch without removing existing plugins

blocks.text: A feature bundle installs several plugins, but one installer rejects its settings. Previously installed capabilities must stay live, and resources created earlier in the failed bundle must be released.
Registering each extension immediately leaves half a bundle visible after failure. A catch that clears the whole registry also removes plugins that were committed before this batch began.

defineHost keeps a use() batch private until it commits. Register draft cleanup through core.onDispose during installation, then await use(draft, broken) to observe completed rollback and the original failure cause.

Both arguments to use(draft, broken) belong to this batch; existing does not. core.onDispose(resource) requires a cleanup resource and accepts ownership during installation. original is a prebuilt local failure object; comparing error.cause === original verifies its identity.
Output:

blocks.code:
PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED true
draft
live

blocks.text: Prints `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED true`, `draft`, then `live`. The wrapper retains the exact TypeError on cause; the failed batch releases its draft resource while the existing registration still works.

Asynchronous use() releases registered failed-batch resources before rejecting; this example acquires one resource. Previously committed registrations stay live. Arbitrary external side effects are not undone, and rollback errors remain secondary detail.

sections.heading: Keep configuration separate from later source mutations

blocks.text: A plugin definition captures application settings, then the caller edits the original settings object before installation. The installed configuration should reflect the captured definition, not that later edit.
A shallow copy only separates the outer object. Nested settings remain shared references, so changing a nested limit can silently alter what a future installer reads.

definePlugin snapshots and recursively freezes admitted configuration data when the definition is created. Pass ordinary data records or arrays; the host later reads its own configuration through config.get(path).

config is optional and defaults to an empty configuration. Here its nested field is settings.limit: 3, captured when the definition is created. The required get path meter.settings.limit selects the plugin, settings record, and limit value. Unknown paths return undefined.
Output:

blocks.code:
3
true true

blocks.text: Prints `3` and `true true` on separate lines. Editing settings.limit to 99 does not change the installed value, and both captured configuration levels are frozen.

Omitted config defaults to an empty configuration. This is not JSON serialization: supported function leaves retain identity, while unsupported prototypes, accessors, symbols, thenables and cycles are rejected. Use host.config.update() for a committed configuration change.

sections.heading: Release plugin resources once in reverse acquisition order

blocks.text: A plugin opens resources in order and depends on later resources being released first. Several callers may also ask the same host to close, so cleanup must not run again for every caller.
Keeping separate teardown lists makes it easy to reverse one list incorrectly or invoke a disposer twice. Calling cleanup from every dispose request multiplies releases of the same resource.

During definePlugin installation, core.onDispose transfers resources to that registration. defineHost memoizes the disposal promise; await it to observe the plugin hook followed by the resource stack.

Each core.onDispose call receives a no-argument cleanup function. The optional definition dispose hook is plugin-level cleanup; an omitted hook adds no step. Host dispose() takes no arguments and memoizes default core cleanup, releasing resources in reverse registration order.
Output:

blocks.code:
true
plugin,second,first
3

blocks.text: Prints `true`, `plugin,second,first`, then `3`. Concurrent dispose calls share one promise, the plugin hook runs before its resources, and another completed dispose call adds no releases.

onDispose admits resources during installation; it is not a general late-registration API. The host collects cleanup failures, and disposeStepTimeoutMs defaults to 5000 ms per step; inspect cleanupComplete and physicalCompletion when cleanup exceeds its budget.

sections.heading: Start providers before consumers regardless of argument order

blocks.text: Two plugins are supplied in UI discovery order, so a consumer can appear before the provider it needs. The consumer still needs the exact provider output, not a separate reconstructed service.

Installing strictly in array order fails when discovery order changes. Rebuilding the dependency inside each consumer avoids the missing value but creates duplicate service state and separate lifetimes.

defineFeature declares synchronous factories and dependency aliases. provider.getFeature() creates a required cross-plugin reference; host.use() validates the graph and starts the provider before resolving the consumer.

defineFeature(factory, dependencies?) requires a synchronous factory. The optional dependency map defaults to empty. summary declares cache as an alias of provider.getFeature("cache"), required by default. features is the optional named Feature map; use(consumer, provider) intentionally reverses installation order.
Output:

blocks.code:
provider -> consumer
true
consumer provider

blocks.text: Prints `provider -> consumer`, `true`, then `consumer provider`. Factories follow dependency order and the consumer receives the exact output object; returned registration handles still follow the input order.

Factories must synchronously return objects, though their methods may be asynchronous. Outputs are frozen per registration; omitted dependencies mean an empty map, and required references must have available providers. This graph orders capabilities, not reactive data changes.

sections.heading: Reject a missing provider before installers run

blocks.text: A deployment enables a consumer plugin but omits its required provider. The host should report the missing prerequisite before the consumer opens any resources.
Looking up services inside the installer discovers the problem only after earlier setup has already performed work. Passing undefined onward shifts the failure into unrelated consumer code.

A reference returned by getFeature() is required by default. defineFeature retains that dependency, and host.use() checks it before installation; count installer calls to make that admission boundary visible.

getFeature("cache") requires a declared name. Without { optional: true }, the reference is required. use(consumer) omits the provider and fails preflight; installs increments only inside the consumer installer.
Output:

blocks.code:
PREREQUISITE_MISSING
0

blocks.text: Prints `PREREQUISITE_MISSING` and `0`. The missing provider is rejected directly by preflight, and the consumer installer is never entered.

Use getFeature(name, { optional: true }) only when the consumer deliberately handles an absent output as undefined. Required and optional references both contribute ordering when a provider exists; this example intentionally uses the required default.

This module owns plugin installation, Feature dependencies, configuration, stage ownership, and cleanup. Applications supply domain behavior. It depends on `@migaia/capability`, `@migaia/lifecycle`, `@migaia/middleware-pipeline`, and `@migaia/utils`. Pipeline execution and stage lifting use middleware-pipeline; lifecycle scopes, mutation queues, and cleanup use lifecycle.

The public entries are `@migaia/plugin-host` and `@migaia/plugin-host/composition`. Do not import internal files. Applications normally use the root Host, plugin, Feature, handle, and error APIs. Composition is a narrow protocol for one composition owner rather than an alternative application Host.

The class `PluginHost<TDomainCore, TValue, TInstalled>` requires its first type parameter, TDomainCore. Its runtime createPluginDomainCore implementation returns an empty object by default. The pipeline value type defaults to `never` and the declared installed tuple to `readonly []`; defineHost separately provides a default domain type. TInstalled informs installation constraints and configuration types. Runtime use() returns an exact input-order handle tuple; it does not change the static type of the Host variable. Published declarations cover the type-only extraction and merging helpers. `IPluginHostCoreFor<THost>` extracts a Host's domain and pipeline axes; type metadata adds no runtime capability.

Simple options or composed functions can suffice for a few static extension points. Use middleware-pipeline directly when only middleware execution is needed. This Host is useful when a library or application needs consistent plugin resources, dependencies, configuration, and reachability. Logger is an existing repository consumer.

sections.heading: Creating a Host and all options

blocks.text: The class entry can override `createPluginDomainCore()` to create a domain core for each installation. The default is an empty object. Domain cores must be ordinary objects with enumerable data properties. They cannot override config, onDispose, or the four use*Pipeline core members. Invalid surfaces retain native TypeError with INVALID_OPTION.

`defineHost(options)` returns one frozen canonical handle. It supports the class behavior and exposes the class-protected useSync and runPipeline methods to the owner holding that handle. Its required `host` field has the same shape as the class constructor options.

rows: Optional; omission returns an empty object. The Host supplies pluginName, zero-based batchIndex, and batch identity

Optional disposal middleware; it must call next itself to include core cleanup. Repeated core disposal shares the original promise
Optional; no domain public members by default, and the fourth type parameter defaults to an empty surface

blocks.text: Own surface descriptors are captured once before Runtime acquisition; accessors remain live. Domain members, Host identity, shared outlets, and fluent pipeline methods belong to the same frozen handle. Canonical Host keys, including identity, take precedence. Composing module should supply their methods here rather than copy a frozen handle. A surface option or descriptor-read failure retains the original through CALLBACK_FAILED. Existing calls with three type parameters remain valid.
The class constructor requires options; defineHost requires the same data under host.

blocks.text: Time values must be finite and non-negative. Invalid options, nonfunction callbacks, or a scheduler without now()/schedule() retain TypeError with INVALID_OPTION. Directly install utils if importing its scheduler entry.

`definePlugin(name, descriptorFactory, features?)` captures a definition without installing it. Each installation synchronously creates one descriptor, then uses its install(), expose(), and featureExpose() hooks. The two expose hooks return synchronous surfaces. Use `definePlugin(definition)` for configuration, setup, update, and disposal hooks. Both forms and valid raw descriptors share admission. Defining them does not execute an installer or Feature factory. Names are required, nonempty, unique within a Host, and cannot contain a dot. Object definitions capture own data fields and are frozen. The retired shared field has no compatibility fallback: migrate cross-plugin capabilities to Features; adapter-owned shared outlets still use their canonical owner protocol.

blocks.text: use(...plugins) accepts a plugin batch. Installation follows dependency order; returned handles follow input order. useSync cannot perform immediate asynchronous installation: a Promise/thenable result causes PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED with INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE on cause, while its eventual rejection stays observed. Immediate installation with setup throws top-level SETUP_REQUIRES_ASYNC_INSTALL before any hook. Constructor options have no plugins field. A class owner calls protected useSync(plugins); the functional handle takes useSync(...plugins). Lazy definitions can be registered synchronously and activated later.

A handle has name, readonly extensions, getFeature(name), and config.get()/update(recipe). Member reads resolve the current registration by name, so an old handle can read a replacement implementation. After removal it throws PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED. An extracted extension function remains bound to its original registration and throws REGISTRATION_REVOKED after revocation. `isPluginHandleCurrent(handle)` instead checks the generation present when that handle was created: disabled and suspended remain current, while replacement, removal, disposal, and unknown objects return false. This probe does not change name-addressed member reads.

Extension results must be ordinary objects. Only enumerable, configurable data properties are published. Accessors and nonconfigurable properties fail with INVALID_OPTION; non-enumerable keys are intentionally skipped with EXTENSION_NON_ENUMERABLE_IGNORED. Do not return a frozen extension object. Host keys, then, and disposal symbols are reserved; catch and finally are allowed. Occupied ordinary keys produce EXTENSION_DUPLICATE; canonical keys take EXTENSION_RESERVED precedence; Object.prototype conflicts produce EXTENSION_OBJECT_PROTOTYPE. Installation retains these failures under PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED. An own then key has its specific INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE classification.

Install/update cores include the domain core plus config.get(), operation, lifecycle, features, featureExpose, onDispose(resource), and four use*Pipeline(stage) methods. Config reads the committed recursively readonly snapshot. Operation supplies its signal and absolute deadlineAt; lifecycle supplies the registration-generation signal. Stage methods return the same core, are install-window-only, and enforce mode compatibility.

core.onDispose takes ownership only during installation. Outside that window it throws RESOURCE_OUTSIDE_INSTALL without acquiring or releasing the supplied resource; the caller still owns it. Resources may be cleanup functions, synchronous disposables, or asynchronous disposables. Their PromiseLike results are assimilated by the lifecycle owner. Synchronous installation may register asynchronous disposers.

Object-form setup runs in this order: domain core → setup → featureExpose → synchronous Feature factories → install. A batch proceeds serially in dependency order. Setup receives only config.get(), operation.{signal,deadlineAt,now()}, lifecycle.signal, and onDispose(resource). It has no Feature outputs, pipeline registration, or Host mutation capability. Its output is passed by identity as the second argument to featureExpose and install. Without setup, those hooks retain their one-core-argument calls.

Setup and subsequent install share the registration's absolute mutation deadline. With no deadline, deadlineAt is undefined; now uses the injected scheduler clock. Success closes the setup registration window without aborting operation.signal. Timeout or Host closure aborts the attempt and rolls back resources. An unsettled setup cannot prevent Host closure. A late result cannot install; a late rejection is reported. Cooperative cancellation echoing the same abort reason is not reported again.

A late setup context.onDispose first attempts to release a valid resource, then throws RESOURCE_OUTSIDE_INSTALL. A resource without a disposer yields INVALID_OPTION. This differs from late core.onDispose ownership. Setup failures in async use, replacement candidates, and prepared composition admissions preserve the original on PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.cause. Lazy activate preserves its original failure identity. Restart diagnostics unwrap only one PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED layer, without stripping other original cause chains.

`defineFeature(factory, dependencies?)` or `defineFeature({ install, dependencies? })` creates an opaque synchronous definition. Dependencies default to an empty map. The factory's core.featureExpose contains explicitly provided capabilities; its second argument contains declared direct dependency aliases. A factory cannot return PromiseLike, though methods of its returned object may be asynchronous. Runtime authority comes from module-owned identity stores, not the type-only __feature field.

definition.getFeature(name) requires a declared name and creates a required reference by default. getFeature(name, { optional: true }) permits undefined when its provider is absent or not activated. A disabled provider still throws PREREQUISITE_DISABLED. handle.getFeature(name) reads the instantiated output. References retain provider name literals; IPluginFeatureName and IPluginFeatureOutput extract names and outputs.

The Host validates required providers and cycles before any installer, then uses dependency order regardless of use argument order. Consumers receive the provider's exact output object, frozen per registration. Cached ordinary output objects and pure functions do not automatically gain revocation guards. Liveness checks belong to handle reads, extension callables, and protected featureExpose entries. Local Feature dependency closures also contribute cross-plugin edges. Missing, disabled, removed, and cyclic prerequisites use top-level PREREQUISITE_MISSING, PREREQUISITE_DISABLED, PREREQUISITE_REMOVED, and DEPENDENCY_CYCLE rather than an installation wrapper.

readPluginDependencies(input) returns a readonly { provider, required } list. It traverses the local closure, preserves first-provider-reference order, and lets required references win over optional duplicates. Inputs may be definitions, valid raw descriptors, or composition admissions. An admission reuses its captured snapshot without rereading getters; other inputs use standard admission once. No setup, installer, or factory runs. Native admission errors keep their exact object, runtime type, and stack.

host.config is a stable facade. Its required get path can be a plugin name, plugin.key, or plugin.[index].key, with further nesting. Unknown plugins or paths return undefined. config.update(name, recipe) requires both arguments and a synchronous partial plain-record result. Missing plugins reject with PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED. handle.config offers the same operations scoped to one plugin.

Initial configuration is copied and recursively frozen. Ordinary records, arrays, and supported primitives are accepted; function leaves retain identity, so this is not a JSON serialization domain. Date, RegExp, Map, Set, class instances, accessors, nested non-enumerable properties, symbols, dangerous proto/constructor/prototype keys, callable then, and cycles are rejected. Repeated acyclic references are not cycles. Invalid values produce INVALID_CONFIG_VALUE; cycles produce CONFIG_CYCLE_REJECTED, with path/reason detail. Writes to frozen snapshots follow native JavaScript behavior without a promised PluginHost code.

Updates copy and freeze patched branches while sharing untouched frozen branches. update(next, core) sees the complete candidate, while core.config.get() still reads committed configuration. Success commits it. Recipe, patch admission, update-hook, and deadline failures preserve config identity, revision, and existing extensions. Unclassified callbacks receive CALLBACK_FAILED while retaining the original object or cause. Valid PromiseLike lifecycle results are assimilated once.

Both get and update require an active Host. Ordinary get entry failures throw synchronously; failures inside update's queue reject its promise. The setup/beforeRelease synchronous guards below still apply.

sections.heading: Disablement, dependency policies, replacement, and lazy activation

blocks.text: await host.plugin.disable(name) returns { token }. await token.enable() restores that exact registration; host.plugin.enable(name) enables by name; disabled() returns a readonly name snapshot. Disablement keeps resources and scopes without disposal. Extensions, Feature outputs, and stages become unreachable, while Host configuration remains readable and updatable. A successful installation first fires onEnable; each later real transition fires its corresponding notification. Notification failures are reported without rolling back state. A dependent cannot enable while its provider remains disabled. A token preflights the full restoration group before enabling any member.

disable and unUse accept { policy?: 'reject' | 'cascade' | 'suspend'; dryRun?: boolean }, defaulting to reject and false. Reject preserves state and exposes all transitive blockers in detail.blockedBy. Cascade includes required dependents. Suspend handles the target while retaining activated dependent instances and resources. Their handles and extracted functions throw PLUGIN_SUSPENDED, and their stages stop participating. Re-enabling the same provider can restore them directly; a new provider with that name follows capability resume planning to rebind, restart, or resume. Whole-Host release remains dependent-first, including suspended registrations.

dryRun: true returns a frozen { policy, order, steps, edges } plan without ok or mutation. Real unUse success and failure both include frozen affected containing only applied steps; failure additionally includes errors. Migration: replace strict equality against the old { ok: true } shape with an ok check and affected inspection. Literal dryRun true selects the plan overload; omission/false selects execution. Branch on a broad boolean first. Retired { cascade: true } is rejected with INVALID_OPTION.

replace(name, next) requires matching names. It installs the candidate first and leaves the old implementation serving if that fails. Publication switches new runs to the new stage generation; existing runs keep old leases. Captured old functions revoke immediately, while name handles resolve the new registration. Disabled state is retained. Activated required dependents can rebind through onDependencyReplaced. Missing or failed hooks cause their required closure to drain and dispose dependent-first, then reinstall topologically, retaining runtime config and prior activation/disablement state. Old generations dispose after draining. Restart failure does not undo the new provider: failed dependents stay removed, and DEPENDENT_RESTART_FAILED retains an AggregateError ordered as restart failure, rebinding errors, then cleanup errors; detail.dependents lists the affected plugins. Secondary cleanup failures stay reported.

Lazy use registers without activation; extensions throw PLUGIN_NOT_ACTIVATED. activate(name) activates required lazy providers before its own installer. Concurrent same-name calls share a promise. Eager installation activates required registered lazy providers; lazy entries used only by lazy members remain cold. Failed preflight activates nothing. Disabled activation yields PLUGIN_DISABLED. Failed activation withdraws attempted stages, extensions, and shared receipts, releases resources, and retains the cold registration/handle. Explicit retry uses a new scope and batch-bound core. Cleanup errors preserve the primary, and late physical work remains observed.

Mutations such as use, unUse, and config.update share lifecycle's FIFO queue. Defaults report waits beyond 1000 ms without a code or rejection. Only a numeric queueAdmissionTimeoutMs removes expired queued work with MUTATION_QUEUE_TIMEOUT. It does not interrupt started work or permanently disable the Host. False disables those timers and reports. Terminal dispose enters the queue without admission-timeout eviction.

Lifecycle hooks, including setup, install, Feature/expose, update, beforeRelease, disposal, enablement, and rebinding, cannot reenter Host mutation. LIFECYCLE_MUTATION is thrown by entry guards on use/unUse/replace/config.update, while asynchronous enablement entries reject their promises. Throughout an awaited setup or beforeRelease window, new mutations are rejected through the same entry-specific form. Work queued before the window remains FIFO and may reach a configured admission deadline.

Synchronous activate reentry is rejected before consulting a shared request. The runtime has no async-context tracking: after an await, same-name activate can share the active promise just like an external caller. Awaiting one's own activation self-deadlocks. A finite mutationTimeoutMs eventually rejects and rolls back with MUTATION_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT; false can leave it pending indefinitely. Start activation outside hooks.

Host stage registration returns this; plugin core registration returns the core. Unsupported lifts synchronously throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH with the upstream middleware-pipeline TypeError / INVALID_OPTION on cause.

Class owners invoke protected runPipeline(value, done) from a domain entry; functional handles expose it directly. Both value and done are required. Sync next records a value and starts downstream after the current stage returns. Async next starts downstream immediately; awaiting it supports after-downstream logic. Omitting next is normal short-circuiting: done is skipped while the run can complete successfully. Duplicate next produces PIPELINE_NEXT_DUPLICATE; late next is ignored and reported as PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE.

Generator modes drain the current stage before passing its ordinary return value onward. Implicit undefined or GENERATOR_HALT stops the chain. GENERATOR_CONTINUE selects the last yield, or the input if nothing yielded. GENERATOR_UNDEFINED forwards an actual undefined payload only when its type permits it. Async-generator awaits serially; it provides neither streaming fan-out nor onion execution. Import modes, stage types, and these unique symbols directly from middleware-pipeline, and install that dependency directly when importing it.

Registering stages while any nested run remains active throws PIPELINE_EXECUTING. A run captures its admitted stages. Host stages and plugin slots follow first-allocation order; disabling, restoring, and replacing retain positions. New runs do not acquire revoked generations; old runs retain their leases until completion or cooperative exit.

All stage modes receive context last; generators receive it second. context.signal is the Host lifecycle signal and aborts when disposal starts. A stage must use it to cancel its own I/O. At stage entry, return, or next dispatch, the runner can stop with HOST_DISPOSING or HOST_DISPOSED; it cannot preempt arbitrary promises. A signal reason and later admission error may have matching semantic identity without being the same object. Ordinary failure wins over simultaneous cancellation; one ordinary failure preserves its object. Async stage/downstream dual failures use AggregateError / PIPELINE_FAILED with [stageError, downstreamError]. Serial async-generator failures from factory, body, or done have no equivalent dual-frame aggregation.

Before an installed registration is released, beforeRelease(context) runs at most once. During ordinary removal its publication still serves existing calls. The context signal belongs to that registration; deadlineAt and remainingMs() use the Host clock and disposeStepTimeoutMs. Disablement, suspension, and cold lazy registration alone do not trigger it. Failure or timeout is collected without rolling removal back. Migration: a nonfunction beforeRelease formerly used as metadata now fails as TypeError / INVALID_OPTION.

Removal withdraws new registration/stage admission, drains the relevant leases, runs the plugin disposer, then releases registered resources in reverse order. Ordinary unUse/dispose uses per-step disposeStepTimeoutMs. Reaching it records DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT and continues without cancelling an active promise. A disposer awaiting the host.dispose that invoked it creates self-waiting; a finite step budget allows logical closure to proceed, while false waits indefinitely.

unUse returns { ok: true, affected } or { ok: false, errors, affected }. Drain timeout records PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT and continues bounded cleanup. Default core dispose shares one promise across repeated calls and synchronous reentry. It returns logicalTerminal, cleanupErrors, cleanupComplete, and possibly physicalCompletion without reopening the Host on cleanup failure. Custom defineHost options.dispose middleware can throw or reject: that failure is classified and rejects the same memoized promise. Core structured cleanup does not guarantee that arbitrary middleware cannot reject.

cleanupComplete false does not mean resources have been released. cleanupErrors is a current snapshot; physicalCompletion carries later errors and may itself have a continuation. To obtain the complete final result, use lifecycle mergeCleanupResults([result]) and install lifecycle directly when importing it. Finite waits do not terminate running leases/disposers; late failures remain observed.

Cleanup functions run directly. Resource objects prefer asynchronous disposal, then synchronous disposal. A plugin's dispose hook takes precedence over symbol cleanup. asyncDisposeKey uses native Symbol.asyncDispose when available, otherwise the module fallback. Synchronous resources can use native Symbol.dispose or ordinary functions, without mandatory polyfills.

isManagedHost(value) recognizes Hosts created by this physical module instance. openComposition(host) accepts those identities, including class and functional Hosts; a lookalike or another installed module copy is not sufficient. The identity writer is private, and defineHost accepts no receiver alias.

A composition owner reads revision/getCurrentSnapshot(), captures definitions with createPluginAdmission, reserves opaque positions with createDataOrderSlot(name), then calls prepareAdmissions([{ admission, slot }]). Setup may execute, but candidate extensions, config, Features, and stages remain unpublished. commitPreparedAdmissions is synchronous without user code and rejects stale revisions. discardPreparedAdmissions rolls temporary resources back once. Returned registration tokens identify exact installations rather than whichever plugin currently has a name.

Calling createDataOrderSlot reserves its order immediately. Disablement, recovery, and replacement reuse it. Retire it only when a definition is permanently removed or the session ends. prepareUnUseBatch accepts exact tokens in the owner's cleanup order. commitPreparedUnUseBatch(prepared, { beforeCleanup? }) first commits logical revocation, then waits for the fence and generation-specific pipeline leases. beforeCleanup is optional without a default promise; when supplied it completes before cleanup.

Managed cleanup requires execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs. A number is shared across the batch's leases and cleanup steps; exhaustion continues later steps even if ordinary disposeStepTimeoutMs is false. Explicit pipelineDrainTimeoutMs false instead waits for actual completion step by step, bypassing ordinary limits. The budget does not revoke running work. Observe all physicalCompletion continuations for physical release, or let the outer realm owner terminate its actual execution environment.

createView(token) exposes only that exact registration's extensions, without Host, config, shared, or mutation capability. Repeated views keep function references and concrete Host receivers. Token views remain valid during disablement; complete Host views reject then and recover their original function references on enablement. Removal revokes both. Foreign or revoked tokens fail closed. Migration: the old root createRegistrationView and IPluginRegistrationReceipt were removed; use composition createView/IRegistrationToken.

inspectFeatures(roots) from composition reads trusted Feature topology without executing factories. Adapter-only getPluginRuntimeIntegration(core) accepts a canonical module core and connects declared shared outlets, Features, and registration lifetimes. It is not an admission bypass for ordinary plugins. Only canonical same-family contributions share a slot; ordinary extensions and other families cannot occupy it. A new shared getter publication on a nonextensible Host preserves native TypeError with PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED and leaves no failed family behind. Ordinary handle extensions retain their existing nonextensible-Host contract.

PluginHostError extends Error with readonly source, code, and optional detail. Its source is @migaia/plugin-host; cause/errors retain original failures. Mutable native callback errors receive identity in place; immutable or non-Error values remain on cause. Complete foreign identities retain their owner. INVALID_OPTION keeps TypeError; configuration-domain and cycle failures are PluginHostError. Do not classify all failures by one class or parse diagnostic text.

Rollback failures do not replace installation failures. PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.detail includes failedName and rollbackErrors in release order. Async use publishes a completed frozen detail; sync useSync publishes a frozen snapshot with detail.completion for final frozen identities. Await completion before translating errors that need all secondary failures. PLUGIN_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED is an additional diagnostic.

diagnostic's third argument retains the original contained failure. Reporter failures cannot alter Host control flow: onDiagnosticFailure receives them, then globalThis.reportError is used if available when that outlet is missing or also fails. Provide onDiagnosticFailure explicitly when Node observation is needed. PluginHostStatus is active/closing/disposed; PluginHostRegistrationLifecycle is idle/install/dispose. blocks.text: The emitted syntax target is ES2020. The host must supply Promise, Map, Symbol, AggregateError, and the native capabilities used. Node, Bun, Deno, Workers, mini-programs, and Electron processes can host it without a framework binding. Browser use, including Chrome/Edge 85+, Firefox 79+, Opera 71+, and Safari 14+, also requires the native APIs used. Disposal symbols remain optional as described above.
The existing scripts below are module gates. test checks dist freshness, builds the module when needed, then runs Vitest. No command is considered passed without actual execution.

blocks.text: For a stalled installation, distinguish queue admission, hook execution, and self-awaiting activation. A failed config update preserves the committed snapshot; inspect code/cause. Use handles returned from use for typed extension access. For unfinished cleanup, inspect its result and continuations rather than assuming logical closure implies physical release.

On sync/async hosts, owners can call `runPipelineSync(value, terminal)` or `runPipelineAsync(value, terminal)` on the `defineHost` handle; subclasses use the same protected entries. Both consume the same registrations, order and lifecycle leases. Sync stages run in both. A visible async stage makes the sync entry throw `ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY` before any stage or terminal runs; removing or disabling it restores sync execution.

The sync entry returns `TResult | undefined`; the async entry accepts a terminal returning `Promise<TResult>` and returns `Promise<TResult | undefined>`. A stage that omits next halts with undefined. Empty lanes invoke the terminal directly, preserving its exact value or Promise identity. Nonempty async execution waits for the actual terminal operation before cleanup. Generator hosts retain `runPipeline`; explicit sync/async entries reject them with `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`.

`getPluginRuntimeIntegration(core).assertPreparedRegistration()` checks the original registration only. Current installation uses original operation admission; a completed candidate in the same unpublished batch requires its exact batch identity and a current installation; published registrations use the original handle admission. Rollback, removal, and host closing revoke access. It returns no registration object and grants no late resource or installation rights. Existing `assertCurrent()` and `core.config.get()` semantics remain unchanged.

blocks.text: 插件定义捕获应用设置后，调用者在安装前修改了原设置对象；安装后的配置应反映定义时的快照，而不是后来的外部修改。
浅拷贝只分离最外层对象，嵌套设置仍为共享引用，修改内层限制会悄悄改变后续安装器读到的内容。
`definePlugin` 在创建定义时对接纳的配置数据做快照并递归冻结，传入普通数据记录或数组，宿主随后通过 `config.get(path)` 读取自己的配置。
`config` 可选、默认空配置，本例字段为 `settings.limit: 3`；定义时捕获嵌套对象。`host.config.get(path)` 的必填路径 `meter.settings.limit` 依次选择插件、设置记录和限制值，未知路径返回 undefined。

guidance.heading: 创建 Host 与全部选项

blocks.text: 类入口可重写 `createPluginDomainCore()`，每次安装创建一份领域 core。默认返回空对象。领域 core 必须是普通对象、可枚举 data property，不能覆盖 `config`、`onDispose` 或四个 `use*Pipeline` core 保留成员；无效表面以原生 TypeError / `INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝。
函数入口 `defineHost(options)` 返回冻结的 canonical handle。它提供与类入口相同的功能，并把类上的 protected `useSync`、`runPipeline` 暴露给持有 handle 的 owner。选项 `host` 必填，形状与类构造选项一致；其余字段如下：

类构造 `options` 必填，defineHost 的 `host` 同样必填：

blocks.text: 所有时间数值须有限、非负；非法选项、非函数回调或不满足 scheduler 协议的对象以 TypeError / `INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝。直接导入 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的消费项目需直接安装 utils。

PluginHostError 继承 Error，携带只读 source、code、可选 detail；source 为 `@migaia/plugin-host`，原始失败通过 cause/errors 可达。可写 native 回调错误原位附身份，不可写或非 Error 值保留在 cause，完整外包身份保留原 owner。INVALID_OPTION 形状错误保留 TypeError；配置值与循环错误是 PluginHostError。不要仅按类名处理所有错误，也不要解析诊断文案。

安装主错不被回滚失败覆盖。PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.detail 包含 failedName、按回滚顺序的 rollbackErrors；异步 use 的 detail 已完成且冻结，同步 useSync 先公布冻结快照，通过 detail.completion 返回最终冻结详情。需要完整次错身份的转换应先 await completion。回滚失败另报 PLUGIN_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED。

diagnostic 的第三参数保留原失败身份；诊断回调自身失败不会改变 Host 控制流，而交给 onDiagnosticFailure，再失败或省略时交给宿主存在的 globalThis.reportError。Node 需要这类观测时显式提供 onDiagnosticFailure。PluginHostStatus 为 active/closing/disposed；PluginHostRegistrationLifecycle 为 idle/install/dispose。ERROR_TEXT 是根命名导出的稳定英文消息表，MiddlewarePipelineMode/Violation 属于 middleware-pipeline。
`PluginHostDisposalNodeKind` 区分清理错误、聚合及 disposer 包装；`readPluginHostDisposalProvenance(error)` 只读取本物理包登记的追溯信息，未知错误或重复包副本返回 undefined，不按形状猜测。它用于诊断，不替代 source/code/cause 分类。

symbols.name: definePlugin
symbols.purpose:
Defines a plugin without running installation hooks. Function form builds a fresh descriptor per registration; object form also declares configuration, setup and lifecycle hooks. Config is captured when defining, not when the caller later mutates it.

Examples pass host.execution.mutationTimeoutMs and pipelineDrainTimeoutMs as 5000 ms: required active-mutation and pipeline-drain budgets, with no defaults; false explicitly removes either deadline. host.config.get(path) uses plugin-name dot paths and returns undefined for an absent path.
symbols.core:
name: Required function-form nonempty name, unique per host and without a dot.
descriptorFactory: Required synchronous function-form callback receiving the install core. Return an object with optional install(), expose() and featureExpose() hooks, all omitted by default. install may be awaitable through use(); expose and featureExpose must be synchronous. install/expose extension keys must be disjoint.
featureRecord: Optional function-form root Feature record; omitted means no roots. Dependencies are declared inside each defineFeature dependency map.
definition: Required object-form own-data definition; fields and hook inputs are documented below.
A plugin definition (`IDefinedPluginConstraint`) with `name`, the declared fields, and `getFeature(name)` for consumers. Invalid fields throw `INVALID_OPTION`; retired fields such as `shared` throw `PLUGIN_DEFINITION_INVALID`.
name: Unique plugin name within a host. It addresses the plugin in `unUse`, `replace`, `config.get("name.key")` and Feature references, so it must not contain `.`.
config: Optional configuration: definePlugin snapshots and recursively freezes it at definition time; installation creates a registration-owned copy. Plain records/arrays and supported primitive or function leaves are admitted, while invalid values and cycles reject. Read core.config.get() or host.config.get(path); commit changes with host.config.update().
Omitted; the public definition.config is undefined and the host uses an empty configuration record.
features: Record of named roots created by defineFeature. Their dependency maps can reference provider.getFeature(name). The host installs required providers first and injects resolved root outputs as core.features.<name>.
Omitted; no Feature roots.
install: Required object-form hook. Receives the domain core plus config, operation, lifecycle, onDispose and pipeline registration methods; declared Feature outputs are ready. Return an extension record, or an awaitable record through asynchronous use(). Own enumerable data properties must be configurable; frozen extension records are rejected.
install.core: Registration-local capabilities. onDispose(resource) is allowed only during install: pass a void/PromiseLike<void> cleanup function or a disposable object; resources are released in reverse order after the plugin disposer.
install.setupOutput: Second argument only when setup is declared; exact resolved setup output. Otherwise install receives only core.
setup: Optional preparation hook before Feature construction and install. Receives config.get(), operation.signal/deadlineAt/now(), lifecycle.signal and onDispose(resource), but no Features or pipeline registration. Its exact resolved result becomes the second install/featureExpose argument.
Omitted; no preparation phase or second hook argument.
featureExpose: Optional object of methods or synchronous hook producing it. Feature factories receive only this explicit read-only method facade, not the whole install core; methods are revoked when the registration ends.
Omitted; an empty expose object.
activation: When the plugin installs: `eager` installs during `use()`; `lazy` only registers it and installs on `host.activate(name)` or when an eager plugin requires it.
`eager`: installed by `use()`.
Install immediately in `use()`.
Register only; install on first `activate()` or when required.
update: Called by `host.config.update(name, recipe)` with the candidate configuration `next` (read-only). Returning normally commits `next`; throwing or rejecting keeps the old configuration.
onEnable: Notification after the plugin becomes reachable: once after install, then after every real `enable`. Failures are only reported through `diagnostic`.
onDisable: Notification after the plugin was disabled (resources are kept). Failures are only reported.
onDependencyReplaced: Called on a dependent when a provider it requires was replaced with `host.replace()`. Rebinding to the new `outputs` here avoids a restart; without this hook (or when it throws) the dependent is restarted.
dispose: Plugin-level cleanup run on removal or host disposal, after `beforeRelease` and before resources registered with `onDispose` are released. Bounded by `disposeStepTimeoutMs`.
beforeRelease: Called once before an installed generation is released, while it can still serve calls; use it to flush or hand off work. `context.signal`, `deadlineAt` and `remainingMs()` describe the time budget. Failures are collected and release continues.
A plugin definition does nothing until installed. After `host.use(plugin)` the host gains: the object returned by `install` (and `expose`) on `handle.extensions` (derived hosts such as Logger also put these methods on the host itself); the pipeline stages the plugin registered; its Features for other plugins; its configuration under `host.config`; and cleanup of every resource it registered when it is removed.
symbols.advanced:
Stages registered with `core.usePipeline*` join every later host pipeline run in first-registration order.
Resources registered with `core.onDispose` or `context.onDispose` are released in reverse order when the plugin is removed or the host is disposed.
Package an optional capability (colored output, remote sink, cache) that users install only when needed.
Open a connection in async `setup`, publish typed methods in `install`, and let removal close it.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content:
Defines a plugin without running installation hooks. Function form builds a fresh descriptor per registration; object form also declares configuration, setup and lifecycle hooks. Config is captured when defining, not when the caller later mutates it.

Examples pass host.execution.mutationTimeoutMs and pipelineDrainTimeoutMs as 5000 ms: required active-mutation and pipeline-drain budgets, with no defaults; false explicitly removes either deadline. host.config.get(path) uses plugin-name dot paths and returns undefined for an absent path.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import definePlugin from @migaia/plugin-host, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use definePlugin when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when definePlugin does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained function example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
name: Required function-form nonempty name, unique per host and without a dot.
descriptorFactory: Required synchronous function-form callback receiving the install core. Return an object with optional install(), expose() and featureExpose() hooks, all omitted by default. install may be awaitable through use(); expose and featureExpose must be synchronous. install/expose extension keys must be disjoint.
featureRecord: Optional function-form root Feature record; omitted means no roots. Dependencies are declared inside each defineFeature dependency map.
definition: Required object-form own-data definition; fields and hook inputs are documented below.
A plugin definition (`IDefinedPluginConstraint`) with `name`, the declared fields, and `getFeature(name)` for consumers. Invalid fields throw `INVALID_OPTION`; retired fields such as `shared` throw `PLUGIN_DEFINITION_INVALID`.
name: Unique plugin name within a host. It addresses the plugin in `unUse`, `replace`, `config.get("name.key")` and Feature references, so it must not contain `.`.
config: Optional configuration: definePlugin snapshots and recursively freezes it at definition time; installation creates a registration-owned copy. Plain records/arrays and supported primitive or function leaves are admitted, while invalid values and cycles reject. Read core.config.get() or host.config.get(path); commit changes with host.config.update().
Omitted; the public definition.config is undefined and the host uses an empty configuration record.
features: Record of named roots created by defineFeature. Their dependency maps can reference provider.getFeature(name). The host installs required providers first and injects resolved root outputs as core.features.<name>.
Omitted; no Feature roots.
install: Required object-form hook. Receives the domain core plus config, operation, lifecycle, onDispose and pipeline registration methods; declared Feature outputs are ready. Return an extension record, or an awaitable record through asynchronous use(). Own enumerable data properties must be configurable; frozen extension records are rejected.
install.core: Registration-local capabilities. onDispose(resource) is allowed only during install: pass a void/PromiseLike<void> cleanup function or a disposable object; resources are released in reverse order after the plugin disposer.
install.setupOutput: Second argument only when setup is declared; exact resolved setup output. Otherwise install receives only core.
setup: Optional preparation hook before Feature construction and install. Receives config.get(), operation.signal/deadlineAt/now(), lifecycle.signal and onDispose(resource), but no Features or pipeline registration. Its exact resolved result becomes the second install/featureExpose argument.
Omitted; no preparation phase or second hook argument.
featureExpose: Optional object of methods or synchronous hook producing it. Feature factories receive only this explicit read-only method facade, not the whole install core; methods are revoked when the registration ends.
Omitted; an empty expose object.
activation: When the plugin installs: `eager` installs during `use()`; `lazy` only registers it and installs on `host.activate(name)` or when an eager plugin requires it.
`eager`: installed by `use()`.
Install immediately in `use()`.
Register only; install on first `activate()` or when required.
update: Called by `host.config.update(name, recipe)` with the candidate configuration `next` (read-only). Returning normally commits `next`; throwing or rejecting keeps the old configuration.
onEnable: Notification after the plugin becomes reachable: once after install, then after every real `enable`. Failures are only reported through `diagnostic`.
onDisable: Notification after the plugin was disabled (resources are kept). Failures are only reported.
onDependencyReplaced: Called on a dependent when a provider it requires was replaced with `host.replace()`. Rebinding to the new `outputs` here avoids a restart; without this hook (or when it throws) the dependent is restarted.
dispose: Plugin-level cleanup run on removal or host disposal, after `beforeRelease` and before resources registered with `onDispose` are released. Bounded by `disposeStepTimeoutMs`.
beforeRelease: Called once before an installed generation is released, while it can still serve calls; use it to flush or hand off work. `context.signal`, `deadlineAt` and `remainingMs()` describe the time budget. Failures are collected and release continues.
A plugin definition does nothing until installed. After `host.use(plugin)` the host gains: the object returned by `install` (and `expose`) on `handle.extensions` (derived hosts such as Logger also put these methods on the host itself); the pipeline stages the plugin registered; its Features for other plugins; its configuration under `host.config`; and cleanup of every resource it registered when it is removed.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
Stages registered with `core.usePipeline*` join every later host pipeline run in first-registration order.
Resources registered with `core.onDispose` or `context.onDispose` are released in reverse order when the plugin is removed or the host is disposed.
Package an optional capability (colored output, remote sink, cache) that users install only when needed.
Open a connection in async `setup`, publish typed methods in `install`, and let removal close it.

guidance.id: 隔离配置与调用者后续修改
guidance.heading: 隔离配置与调用者后续修改

blocks.text: 插件定义捕获应用设置后，调用者在安装前修改了原设置对象；安装后的配置应反映定义时的快照，而不是后来的外部修改。
浅拷贝只分离最外层对象，嵌套设置仍为共享引用，修改内层限制会悄悄改变后续安装器读到的内容。
`definePlugin` 在创建定义时对接纳的配置数据做快照并递归冻结，传入普通数据记录或数组，宿主随后通过 `config.get(path)` 读取自己的配置。
`config` 可选、默认空配置，本例字段为 `settings.limit: 3`；定义时捕获嵌套对象。`host.config.get(path)` 的必填路径 `meter.settings.limit` 依次选择插件、设置记录和限制值，未知路径返回 undefined。
输出：

blocks.code:
3
true true

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `3`、`true true`；把外部 `settings.limit` 改为 `99` 没有改变安装值，捕获配置的两层对象也均已冻结。
省略 `config` 时使用空配置，这不是 JSON 序列化：支持的函数叶值保留身份，不支持的原型、访问器、符号、类 `Promise` 对象（带可调用 `then` 的对象）与环会被拒绝，已提交配置应通过 `host.config.update()` 修改。

members.description: 插件卸载存在清理失败。

members.signature: readonly EXTENSION_NON_ENUMERABLE_IGNORED: (name: string, key: PropertyKey) => string;
members.description: 诊断：install() 返回值上一个非枚举键被跳过挂载（不是错误，是有意的行为，但必须可观测）。

members.name: DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT
members.signature: readonly DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT: (phase: string, waitedMs: number) => string;
members.description: 正式 SLA：单个 disposer（pipeline disposer / 插件 dispose 钩子 / resource disposer） 等待超过阈值仍未 settle，包括该 * disposer 反过来 await 了同一次 dispose() 调用自身这种 循环等待。不会中断 disposer 的执行（JS 无法安全撤销已经在跑的 Promise 链），只是停止 * 等待并把这一步计为失败，让整个 dispose 事务仍能收敛到 disposed。

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Canonical English error text and message factories exported by the root entry. Downstream diagnostic adapters can reuse stable Host wording; error handling still branches on source/code rather than comparing message text.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import ERROR_TEXT from @migaia/plugin-host, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use ERROR_TEXT when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when ERROR_TEXT does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content: Canonical English error text and message factories exported by the root entry. Downstream diagnostic adapters can reuse stable Host wording; error handling still branches on source/code rather than comparing message text.

blocks.text: PluginHostError 继承 Error，携带只读 source、code、可选 detail；source 为 `@migaia/plugin-host`，原始失败通过 cause/errors 可达。可写 native 回调错误原位附身份，不可写或非 Error 值保留在 cause，完整外包身份保留原 owner。INVALID_OPTION 形状错误保留 TypeError；配置值与循环错误是 PluginHostError。不要仅按类名处理所有错误，也不要解析诊断文案。

安装主错不被回滚失败覆盖。PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.detail 包含 failedName、按回滚顺序的 rollbackErrors；异步 use 的 detail 已完成且冻结，同步 useSync 先公布冻结快照，通过 detail.completion 返回最终冻结详情。需要完整次错身份的转换应先 await completion。回滚失败另报 PLUGIN_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED。

diagnostic 的第三参数保留原失败身份；诊断回调自身失败不会改变 Host 控制流，而交给 onDiagnosticFailure，再失败或省略时交给宿主存在的 globalThis.reportError。Node 需要这类观测时显式提供 onDiagnosticFailure。PluginHostStatus 为 active/closing/disposed；PluginHostRegistrationLifecycle 为 idle/install/dispose。ERROR_TEXT 是根命名导出的稳定英文消息表，MiddlewarePipelineMode/Violation 属于 middleware-pipeline。
`PluginHostDisposalNodeKind` 区分清理错误、聚合及 disposer 包装；`readPluginHostDisposalProvenance(error)` 只读取本物理包登记的追溯信息，未知错误或重复包副本返回 undefined，不按形状猜测。它用于诊断，不替代 source/code/cause 分类。

请求了未声明的 Feature 名称。
必需 provider 从未安装，安装前直接拒绝。

必需 provider 已卸载，需要重新安装。
Feature 跨插件引用成环，任何 install 前拒绝。
变更会遗留必需依赖者，detail.blockedBy 列出传递闭包。
替换候选名称不同，未安装候选。
新 provider 已提交但依赖者重装失败，cause.errors 首项为重装失败。
退役或不支持的定义字段、非法依赖或非 canonical core，保留 TypeError。
安装/发布失败，原错在 cause，回滚详情保留次错。
即时 useSync 安装遇到 setup，改用异步 use。

扩展使用 Host 协议键、then 或清理 symbol。

构造时 mode 非四种合法值。
stage 无法提升到 Host 模式，cause 保留上游 TypeError。
同次 stage 重复调用 next，不重复派发。

管线执行期间注册新 stage。
async 双失败，AggregateError.errors 固定为 stage、downstream。
已配置准入期限且排队到限，任务移出并不再执行。
beforeRelease 或普通释放步骤超预算，结束等待并继续清理，不强行取消。
入参形状不合法，保留原生 TypeError，修正输入。
配置不满足普通数据语法，detail 含 path/reason。
配置含引用环，提供无环值图。
未分类配置、surface 读取或 defineHost disposal 回调失败；保留原错或 cause。
hook 执行到限，丧失提交权限，迟到结果不能提交。
已取出的扩展属于已卸载或替换的旧注册。
普通卸载排空超预算，ok false，继续有界清理并诊断。
逻辑关闭已提交，清理有错或仍未完成；读取结果与 continuation。
组合目标非本物理包登记的 Host，不做结构兼容。

symbols.core:
name: Unique plugin name within a host. It addresses the plugin in `unUse`, `replace`, `config.get("name.key")` and Feature references, so it must not contain `.`.
config: Optional configuration: definePlugin snapshots and recursively freezes it at definition time; installation creates a registration-owned copy. Plain records/arrays and supported primitive or function leaves are admitted, while invalid values and cycles reject. Read core.config.get() or host.config.get(path); commit changes with host.config.update().
Omitted; the public definition.config is undefined and the host uses an empty configuration record.
features: Record of named roots created by defineFeature. Their dependency maps can reference provider.getFeature(name). The host installs required providers first and injects resolved root outputs as core.features.<name>.
Omitted; no Feature roots.
install: Required object-form hook. Receives the domain core plus config, operation, lifecycle, onDispose and pipeline registration methods; declared Feature outputs are ready. Return an extension record, or an awaitable record through asynchronous use(). Own enumerable data properties must be configurable; frozen extension records are rejected.
install.core: Registration-local capabilities. onDispose(resource) is allowed only during install: pass a void/PromiseLike<void> cleanup function or a disposable object; resources are released in reverse order after the plugin disposer.
install.setupOutput: Second argument only when setup is declared; exact resolved setup output. Otherwise install receives only core.
setup: Optional preparation hook before Feature construction and install. Receives config.get(), operation.signal/deadlineAt/now(), lifecycle.signal and onDispose(resource), but no Features or pipeline registration. Its exact resolved result becomes the second install/featureExpose argument.
Omitted; no preparation phase or second hook argument.
featureExpose: Optional object of methods or synchronous hook producing it. Feature factories receive only this explicit read-only method facade, not the whole install core; methods are revoked when the registration ends.
Omitted; an empty expose object.
activation: When the plugin installs: `eager` installs during `use()`; `lazy` only registers it and installs on `host.activate(name)` or when an eager plugin requires it.
`eager`: installed by `use()`.
Install immediately in `use()`.
Register only; install on first `activate()` or when required.
update: Called by `host.config.update(name, recipe)` with the candidate configuration `next` (read-only). Returning normally commits `next`; throwing or rejecting keeps the old configuration.
onEnable: Notification after the plugin becomes reachable: once after install, then after every real `enable`. Failures are only reported through `diagnostic`.
onDisable: Notification after the plugin was disabled (resources are kept). Failures are only reported.
onDependencyReplaced: Called on a dependent when a provider it requires was replaced with `host.replace()`. Rebinding to the new `outputs` here avoids a restart; without this hook (or when it throws) the dependent is restarted.
dispose: Plugin-level cleanup run on removal or host disposal, after `beforeRelease` and before resources registered with `onDispose` are released. Bounded by `disposeStepTimeoutMs`.
beforeRelease: Called once before an installed generation is released, while it can still serve calls; use it to flush or hand off work. `context.signal`, `deadlineAt` and `remainingMs()` describe the time budget. Failures are collected and release continues.
getFeature: Creates a reference to one Feature this plugin declares, for use in another plugin `defineFeature(factory, { name: reference })`. The reference makes this plugin a provider the consumer depends on.
getFeature.name: Name of a Feature in this plugin `features` record.
getFeature.options: `{ optional: true }` makes the dependency optional: the consumer installs even without this provider.

symbols.purpose: The object returned by defineHost, combining host operations with the application members supplied through surface. It is frozen, so callers cannot add, remove or reassign its own properties. Getters still run on each read and can show current state. TPublicSurface, the fourth generic parameter, describes application members and defaults to no additional members. The host identity belongs to this same object, and use*Pipeline methods return it for chaining. A stage is one function in the host processing pipeline. Stages registered by the host stay until host disposal removes them. Register stages before running the pipeline; registration during a run throws PIPELINE_EXECUTING, meaning that the active pipeline cannot be changed.
symbols.core:
identity: Immutable host identity `{ name, id }`: `name` from the `identity` option, `id` unique per host; used in errors and diagnostics.
plugin: Enable/disable controls: `plugin.disable(name)` hides a plugin (extensions, Features, stages) without releasing resources, `plugin.enable(name)` restores it in place, `plugin.disabled()` lists disabled names.
pipelineMode: Pipeline mode fixed at construction: `sync`, `async`, `generator` or `async-generator`.
revision: Counter of committed installation, removal, replacement, configuration, enablement, stage-registration and terminal changes. Composition owners compare revision to detect stale snapshots; it remains readable after disposal.
config: Per-plugin configuration store. `config.get("plugin.key")` reads a frozen snapshot (unknown paths return `undefined`); `config.update(name, recipe)` merges a patch copy-on-write and commits only after the plugin `update` hook succeeds.
useSync: Installs synchronously and returns handles in input order. A declared setup immediately throws SETUP_REQUIRES_ASYNC_INSTALL. A thenable install result rejects as PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED with INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE on cause; its later rejection is reported through the diagnostic third argument, not inserted retroactively into the immediate cause chain.
useSync.plugins: Plugin definitions with synchronous install.
The handle tuple in input order.
Building a host that must be usable right after construction.
use: Installs one or more plugins as one batch, in Feature dependency order (argument order does not matter). Either every plugin is published or the batch is rolled back in reverse order.
use.plugins: Definitions from `definePlugin()` or plugin factories such as `level()`. Names must be unique and must not contain `.`.
A Promise of the handle tuple in input order. Install failures reject with `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED` (original error on `cause`, `detail.failedName`); missing providers throw `PREREQUISITE_*` directly.
Plugins with async `setup` or `install`, or plugins added at runtime.
unUse: Removes a plugin: runs its `beforeRelease`, waits for running pipelines, withdraws extensions, Features and stages, then runs its disposers and releases resources in reverse order.
unUse.name: Name of the installed plugin.
unUse.options: `policy`: what happens to plugins that require it (`reject` default, `cascade`, `suspend`); `dryRun: true` returns the plan without changing anything.
{ ok: true, affected }, or { ok: false, errors, affected } after cleanup failure or PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. Ordinary unUse continues bounded cleanup after a drain timeout, records/reports that failure and adds no physicalCompletion protocol. dryRun:true returns IPluginDependencyPlan.
activate: Installs a plugin that was registered with `activation: "lazy"`, first activating any lazy providers it requires. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a failure leaves it registered so it can be retried.
activate.name: Name of the lazy plugin.
The handle of the activated plugin; the original install error on failure.
Defer expensive plugins until the first request needs them.
replace: Hot-swaps a plugin: installs `next` first (the old one keeps serving if that fails), then rebinds dependents that implement `onDependencyReplaced` and restarts the others; the old generation is disposed after its running pipelines drain.
replace.name: Name of the installed plugin.
replace.next: New definition with the same name (otherwise `REPLACE_NAME_MISMATCH`).
The handle of the new generation. Old extracted extension functions throw `REGISTRATION_REVOKED`; a failed dependent restart throws `DEPENDENT_RESTART_FAILED` after the replacement took effect.
runPipeline: Runs `value` through host and plugin stages and calls `done` with the final value. Only the holder of a `defineHost()` handle can call it (subclasses use the protected method), so the domain decides when the pipeline runs.
runPipeline.value: Input value.
runPipeline.done: Final callback; not called when a stage stops the value.
`void` in sync modes, a Promise in async modes; host disposal aborts the run with `HOST_DISPOSING`.
runPipelineSync: Runs original synchronous stages from the same canonical lane. Any visible async stage throws ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY before effects. Available on sync/async owner handles or as a protected subclass entry; generator hosts keep runPipeline.
runPipelineSync.value: Input value.
runPipelineSync.done: Terminal returning TResult.
TResult | undefined; halted stages return undefined. Empty lanes preserve the exact terminal value.
runPipelineAsync: Runs async forms of the same stage registrations, including lifted sync stages. Waits for the real terminal Promise and onion cleanup; uses the existing host cancellation and leases.
runPipelineAsync.value: Input value.
runPipelineAsync.done: Terminal returning Promise<TResult>.
Promise<TResult | undefined>. A halted stage resolves undefined; an empty lane returns the original terminal Promise by identity.
dispose: Closes permanently: stops new changes, drains pipelines and releases plugins with dependents first. The completion Promise is published before callbacks or abort listeners run; concurrent or reentrant disposal shares it, so cleanup middleware runs once. The lifecycle abort reason and later admission failure can be distinct instances with the same source/code.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult`: `cleanupErrors` lists cleanup failures; `cleanupComplete: false` means some cleanup is still running, observe `physicalCompletion`.
usePipeline: Adds a synchronous processing function to the host pipeline. Receive the current value and call next(newValue) to continue with a value for the next function. Omitting next() stops processing. The host adapts this synchronous function to its selected mode, so this registration method works in every host mode.
usePipeline.stage: Sync stage; call `next(value)` to continue, omit it to stop the value.
The host itself, so calls can be chained.
useAsyncPipeline: Adds an asynchronous processing function. Call await next(value) to wait for later functions, then perform any work that must happen after them. This is often called onion-style execution because functions wrap later work. The host must use async mode; another mode makes registration throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (value, next) => { await next(value) }`; code after `await next()` runs after downstream.
The host itself.
useGeneratorPipeline: Adds a synchronous generator: a function that produces values step by step with yield. Use it when processing is written in that form. The host accepts it in generator mode and adapts it in async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: `function* (value)`; return a value or a `GENERATOR_*` signal.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Adds an asynchronous generator, which can wait for asynchronous work and produce values with yield. Use it for processing written as async function*. The host must use async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: `async function* (value)`; drained completely before the next stage.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: The object returned by defineHost, combining host operations with the application members supplied through surface. It is frozen, so callers cannot add, remove or reassign its own properties. Getters still run on each read and can show current state. TPublicSurface, the fourth generic parameter, describes application members and defaults to no additional members. The host identity belongs to this same object, and use*Pipeline methods return it for chaining. A stage is one function in the host processing pipeline. Stages registered by the host stay until host disposal removes them. Register stages before running the pipeline; registration during a run throws PIPELINE_EXECUTING, meaning that the active pipeline cannot be changed.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
identity: Immutable host identity `{ name, id }`: `name` from the `identity` option, `id` unique per host; used in errors and diagnostics.
plugin: Enable/disable controls: `plugin.disable(name)` hides a plugin (extensions, Features, stages) without releasing resources, `plugin.enable(name)` restores it in place, `plugin.disabled()` lists disabled names.
pipelineMode: Pipeline mode fixed at construction: `sync`, `async`, `generator` or `async-generator`.
revision: Counter of committed installation, removal, replacement, configuration, enablement, stage-registration and terminal changes. Composition owners compare revision to detect stale snapshots; it remains readable after disposal.
config: Per-plugin configuration store. `config.get("plugin.key")` reads a frozen snapshot (unknown paths return `undefined`); `config.update(name, recipe)` merges a patch copy-on-write and commits only after the plugin `update` hook succeeds.
useSync: Installs synchronously and returns handles in input order. A declared setup immediately throws SETUP_REQUIRES_ASYNC_INSTALL. A thenable install result rejects as PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED with INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE on cause; its later rejection is reported through the diagnostic third argument, not inserted retroactively into the immediate cause chain.
useSync.plugins: Plugin definitions with synchronous install.
The handle tuple in input order.
Building a host that must be usable right after construction.
use: Installs one or more plugins as one batch, in Feature dependency order (argument order does not matter). Either every plugin is published or the batch is rolled back in reverse order.
use.plugins: Definitions from `definePlugin()` or plugin factories such as `level()`. Names must be unique and must not contain `.`.
A Promise of the handle tuple in input order. Install failures reject with `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED` (original error on `cause`, `detail.failedName`); missing providers throw `PREREQUISITE_*` directly.
Plugins with async `setup` or `install`, or plugins added at runtime.
unUse: Removes a plugin: runs its `beforeRelease`, waits for running pipelines, withdraws extensions, Features and stages, then runs its disposers and releases resources in reverse order.
unUse.name: Name of the installed plugin.
unUse.options: `policy`: what happens to plugins that require it (`reject` default, `cascade`, `suspend`); `dryRun: true` returns the plan without changing anything.
{ ok: true, affected }, or { ok: false, errors, affected } after cleanup failure or PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. Ordinary unUse continues bounded cleanup after a drain timeout, records/reports that failure and adds no physicalCompletion protocol. dryRun:true returns IPluginDependencyPlan.
activate: Installs a plugin that was registered with `activation: "lazy"`, first activating any lazy providers it requires. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a failure leaves it registered so it can be retried.
activate.name: Name of the lazy plugin.
The handle of the activated plugin; the original install error on failure.
Defer expensive plugins until the first request needs them.
replace: Hot-swaps a plugin: installs `next` first (the old one keeps serving if that fails), then rebinds dependents that implement `onDependencyReplaced` and restarts the others; the old generation is disposed after its running pipelines drain.
replace.name: Name of the installed plugin.
replace.next: New definition with the same name (otherwise `REPLACE_NAME_MISMATCH`).
The handle of the new generation. Old extracted extension functions throw `REGISTRATION_REVOKED`; a failed dependent restart throws `DEPENDENT_RESTART_FAILED` after the replacement took effect.
runPipeline: Runs `value` through host and plugin stages and calls `done` with the final value. Only the holder of a `defineHost()` handle can call it (subclasses use the protected method), so the domain decides when the pipeline runs.
runPipeline.value: Input value.
runPipeline.done: Final callback; not called when a stage stops the value.
`void` in sync modes, a Promise in async modes; host disposal aborts the run with `HOST_DISPOSING`.
runPipelineSync: Runs original synchronous stages from the same canonical lane. Any visible async stage throws ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY before effects. Available on sync/async owner handles or as a protected subclass entry; generator hosts keep runPipeline.
runPipelineSync.value: Input value.
runPipelineSync.done: Terminal returning TResult.
TResult | undefined; halted stages return undefined. Empty lanes preserve the exact terminal value.
runPipelineAsync: Runs async forms of the same stage registrations, including lifted sync stages. Waits for the real terminal Promise and onion cleanup; uses the existing host cancellation and leases.
runPipelineAsync.value: Input value.
runPipelineAsync.done: Terminal returning Promise<TResult>.
Promise<TResult | undefined>. A halted stage resolves undefined; an empty lane returns the original terminal Promise by identity.
dispose: Closes permanently: stops new changes, drains pipelines and releases plugins with dependents first. The completion Promise is published before callbacks or abort listeners run; concurrent or reentrant disposal shares it, so cleanup middleware runs once. The lifecycle abort reason and later admission failure can be distinct instances with the same source/code.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult`: `cleanupErrors` lists cleanup failures; `cleanupComplete: false` means some cleanup is still running, observe `physicalCompletion`.
usePipeline: Adds a synchronous processing function to the host pipeline. Receive the current value and call next(newValue) to continue with a value for the next function. Omitting next() stops processing. The host adapts this synchronous function to its selected mode, so this registration method works in every host mode.
usePipeline.stage: Sync stage; call `next(value)` to continue, omit it to stop the value.
The host itself, so calls can be chained.
useAsyncPipeline: Adds an asynchronous processing function. Call await next(value) to wait for later functions, then perform any work that must happen after them. This is often called onion-style execution because functions wrap later work. The host must use async mode; another mode makes registration throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (value, next) => { await next(value) }`; code after `await next()` runs after downstream.
The host itself.
useGeneratorPipeline: Adds a synchronous generator: a function that produces values step by step with yield. Use it when processing is written in that form. The host accepts it in generator mode and adapts it in async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: `function* (value)`; return a value or a `GENERATOR_*` signal.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Adds an asynchronous generator, which can wait for asynchronous work and produce values with yield. Use it for processing written as async function*. The host must use async-generator mode; other modes reject registration with PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: `async function* (value)`; drained completely before the next stage.
